item.title: [BM] MOE Pertimbang Hidupkan Semula PdPR Sebagai Tindak Balas Krisis Minyak — Kerana Tiada Yang Lebih 'Jimat' Dari Hantar Anak Balik Ke Laptop
item.description:
Said by: Mohd Azam Ahmad, Education Director-General (under Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek)

Category: Education

Date: 2026-03-15

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Pada 15 Mac, Ketua Pengarah Pendidikan Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad mengumumkan Kementerian Pendidikan akan mengadakan mesyuarat khas minggu depan, dipengerusikan Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek, untuk mengkaji pelaksanaan mekanisme Bekerja Dari Rumah (WFH) dan Pengajaran dan Pembelajaran di Rumah (PdPR) sebagai sebahagian tindak balas penjimatan kerajaan terhadap krisis minyak global. Apabila ditanya sama ada dasar penjimatan itu akan melibatkan sekolah dan pelajar — bermakna menghidupkan semula PdPR era COVID — Mohd Azam berkata “kajian lanjut diperlukan” dan kementerian akan “mengkaji sama ada ada rasional untuk melibatkan sekolah.”

item.title: [BM] Wong Kah Woh Kata KPM Kaji Semula PdPR Untuk Pelajar Ketika Krisis Minyak — Tiga Tahun Reformasi, Dan Budak-Budak Mungkin Kena Balik Kelas Zoom
item.description:
Said by: Wong Kah Woh, Deputy Education Minister (DAP)

Category: Education

Date: 2026-03-15

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Timbalan Menteri Pendidikan Wong Kah Woh memberitahu wartawan di majlis berbuka puasa di Taman Tasik Taiping pada 15 Mac bahawa Kementerian Pendidikan akan menjalankan “kajian menyeluruh” terhadap PdPR — Pengajaran dan Pembelajaran dari Rumah — untuk pelajar sekolah dan kakitangan awam kementerian. Wong berkata kementerian akan memastikan “sebarang keputusan yang diambil tidak menjejaskan murid dan pelajar.” Ini susulan pengesahan Ketua Pengarah Pendidikan Mohd Azam Ahmad sehari sebelumnya bahawa Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek akan mempengerusikan mesyuarat khas minggu depan untuk mengkaji semula mekanisme WFH dan PdPR, menunggu keputusan muktamad Kabinet. KPP mengakui KPM akan “memanfaatkan pengalaman WFH semasa pandemik Covid-19” untuk membentuk strategi.

item.title: MOE Considers Reviving Home-Based Learning as Oil Crisis Response — Because Nothing Says 'Austerity' Like Sending Kids Back to Their Laptops
item.description:
Said by: Mohd Azam Ahmad, Education Director-General (under Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek)

Category: Education

Date: 2026-03-15

📌 What Happened

On March 15, Education Director-General Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad announced the Ministry of Education will hold a special meeting next week, chaired by Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek, to review the implementation of Work From Home and Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) mechanisms as part of the government’s austerity response to the global oil crisis. When asked whether the savings policy would extend to schools and students — effectively reviving the COVID-era PdPR system — Mohd Azam said “further study is required” and that the ministry would “examine whether there is a rationale to involve schools.”

item.title: Wong Kah Woh Says MOE Reviewing PdPR for Students Amid Oil Crisis — Three Years of Reform, and Kids Might Go Back to Zoom School
item.description:
Said by: Wong Kah Woh, Deputy Education Minister (DAP)

Category: Education

Date: 2026-03-15

📌 What Happened

Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh told reporters at a breaking-of-fast event at Taiping Lake Gardens on March 15 that the Ministry of Education will conduct a “comprehensive review” of PdPR — Teaching and Learning from Home — for school students and ministry civil servants. Wong said the ministry would ensure “any decision taken will not adversely affect pupils and students.” This follows Education Director-General Mohd Azam Ahmad’s confirmation the day before that Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek will chair a special meeting next week to review WFH and PdPR mechanisms, pending the Cabinet’s final decision. The DG acknowledged that the MOE would “leverage its experience with WFH during the Covid-19 pandemic” to develop a strategy.

item.title: [BM] Fadhlina Kata Kementerian 'Memantau' Sekolah Dari Ekstremisme — Selepas Polis Sudah Tangkap Enam Remaja Berkaitan IS
item.description:
Said by: Fadhlina Sidek, Education Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2026-03-12

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Pada 12 Mac, Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek memberitahu pemberita di Bukit Mertajam bahawa Kementerian Pendidikan sedang “memantau penglibatan pelajar di institusi pendidikan” untuk menghalang ideologi ekstremis daripada menular ke sekolah. Beliau berkata kementerian telah “menyerahkan perkara itu kepada pihak berkuasa berkaitan untuk siasatan lanjut dan tindakan sewajarnya,” sambil menekankan kerjasama rapat dengan agensi penguatkuasaan untuk melindungi pelajar daripada pengaruh “terutamanya yang berkait rapat dengan Daesh dan keganasan.” Kenyataan ini dibuat berminggu-minggu selepas Cawangan Khas menangkap enam remaja lelaki berusia 16 hingga 21 tahun pada 14–15 Februari dalam operasi khas atas syak terlibat dalam aktiviti IS.

item.title: [BM] Fadhlina Kata Kementerian 'Memantau' Sekolah Terhadap Ekstremisme — Selepas Polis Sudah Tangkap Enam Remaja Berkait IS
item.description:
Said by: Fadhlina Sidek, Education Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2026-03-12

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Pada 12 Mac, Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek memberitahu wartawan di Bukit Mertajam bahawa Kementerian Pendidikan “memantau rapat penglibatan pelajar di institusi pendidikan” bagi mencegah ideologi ekstremis daripada menusuk masuk sekolah. Beliau berkata kementerian telah “menyerahkan perkara itu kepada pihak berkuasa yang berkaitan untuk siasatan lanjut dan tindakan perlu,” dan menekankan kerjasama rapat dengan agensi penguatkuasaan untuk melindungi pelajar daripada pengaruh “terutamanya yang berkait rapat dengan Daesh dan keganasan.” Ini datang berminggu-minggu selepas Cawangan Khas menangkap enam remaja lelaki berumur 16 hingga 21 tahun pada 14–15 Februari dalam operasi seluruh negara atas disyaki penglibatan dalam aktiviti IS.

item.title: Fadhlina Says Ministry Is 'Monitoring' Schools for Extremism — After Police Already Arrested Six Teenagers Linked to IS
item.description:
Said by: Fadhlina Sidek, Education Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2026-03-12

📌 What Happened

On March 12, Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek told reporters in Bukit Mertajam that the Ministry of Education is “closely monitoring student involvement in educational institutions” to prevent extremist ideologies from infiltrating schools. She said the ministry has “left the matter to the relevant authorities for further investigation and necessary action,” and emphasized close cooperation with enforcement agencies to protect students from influence “especially those closely linked to Daesh and terrorism.” This came weeks after the Special Branch arrested six teenage boys aged 16 to 21 on February 14–15 in a nationwide operation over suspected involvement in IS activities.

item.title: [BM] Pelajar Tunjuk Kad Merah Kepada Adam Adli Atas Janji AUKU Yang Dimungkiri — Anak Emas PH Sendiri Jadi Pemungkir
item.description:
Said by: Adam Adli Abdul Halim, Deputy Higher Education Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2026-02-09

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Pada 9 Februari 2026, pelajar universiti berarak ke Parlimen menuntut pemansuhan Akta Universiti dan Kolej Universiti 1971 (AUKU). Sasaran mereka? Timbalan Menteri Pengajian Tinggi Adam Adli Abdul Halim — pernah menjadi aktivis pelajar paling terkenal Malaysia, kini penjelmaan hidup janji PH yang dimungkiri. Memansuhkan AUKU merupakan janji manifesto utama Pakatan Harapan dalam PRU14 (2018) dan PRU15 (2022). Pada lewat Januari 2026, Menteri Pengajian Tinggi Zambry Abd Kadir memberitahu Parlimen kerajaan “tidak bercadang” memansuhkan AUKU — pembalikan dasar yang disampaikan tanpa gembar-gembur. Pelajar menunjukkan kad merah kepada Adam Adli dan memanggilnya “pemungkir.” Zambry enggan menerima memorandum mereka. Adam Adli, 33, ditahan pada 2013 kerana menurunkan bendera di perhimpunan pelajar — tindakan yang menjadikannya simbol gerakan pelajar. PH memperjuangkan kesnya sebagai bukti AUKU tidak adil. Kini beliau duduk dalam kementerian yang menguatkuasakannya.

item.title: Students Flash Red Cards at Adam Adli Over Broken UUCA Promise — PH's Own Poster Boy Turns Reneger
item.description:
Said by: Adam Adli Abdul Halim, Deputy Higher Education Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2026-02-09

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: On 9 February 2026, university students marched to Parliament demanding the abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA). Their target? Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abdul Halim — once Malaysia’s most famous student activist, now the living embodiment of PH’s broken promise. Abolishing UUCA was a key manifesto promise by Pakatan Harapan in both GE14 (2018) and GE15 (2022). In late January 2026, Higher Education Minister Zambry Abd Kadir told Parliament the government had “no plans” to abolish UUCA — a policy reversal delivered without fanfare. Students flashed red cards at Adam Adli and called him a “reneger.” Zambry refused to receive their memorandum. Adam Adli, 33, was arrested in 2013 for lowering a flag at a student rally — an act that made him a symbol of the student movement. PH championed his case as proof that UUCA was unjust. Now he sits in the ministry that enforces it.

item.title: [BM] Bahasa Melayu dan Sejarah Wajib Merentas SEMUA Sistem Pendidikan — Pengkritik Kata Ia Menyekat Kepelbagaian
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2026-01-21

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Pada Januari 2026, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim mengumumkan bahawa Bahasa Melayu dan Sejarah akan diwajibkan merentas semua sistem pendidikan di Malaysia — termasuk sekolah vernakular (SJKC dan SJKT), sekolah antarabangsa, dan institusi swasta. Anwar berkata keperluan ini bertujuan “mengukuhkan kedudukan Bahasa Melayu sebagai bahasa kebangsaan” dan memberikan “pemahaman bersama tentang sejarah negara.” Pengkritik berhujah bahawa ini menjejaskan perlindungan perlembagaan untuk pendidikan vernakular di bawah Perkara 152(1)(a) dan menyekat kepelbagaian yang menjadikan sistem pendidikan Malaysia unik. Analisis mendalam CNA menyatakan “politik dan kesukaran” pembaharuan pendidikan Malaysia, menggambarkan bagaimana “bahasa dan agama” kekal sebagai bidang dasar paling mudah terbakar.

item.title: Mandatory Malay and History Across ALL Education Systems — Critics Say It Stifles Diversity
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2026-01-21

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: In January 2026, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that Bahasa Melayu and History would be mandatory across all education systems in Malaysia — including vernacular schools (SJKC and SJKT), international schools, and private institutions. Anwar said the requirement aims to “bolster the status of Bahasa Melayu as the national language” and provide “a common understanding of national history.” Critics argued this undermines constitutional protections for vernacular education under Article 152(1)(a) and stifles the diversity that makes Malaysia’s education system unique. CNA’s in-depth analysis noted the “politics and difficulties” of Malaysian education reform, describing how “language and religion” remain the most combustible policy areas.

item.title: [BM] Kes Buli Sekolah Melonjak 17% — 7,681 Kes Pada 2024 Meskipun 'Reformasi'

Said by: Fadhlina Sidek, Education Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2025-10-18

Schools recorded 7,681 bullying cases in 2024, up from 6,528 in 2023 — a 17% increase. Teachers report students are ‘ruder, more restless, less curious.’ Education Ministry’s disciplinary reforms are clearly not working.

item.title: [BM] Sistem Persekolahan Malaysia Dalam 'Kemerosotan' — Pelajar Lebih Biadap, Kurang Ingin Tahu, Guru Terbeban
item.description:
Said by: FMT Opinion / Teachers

Category: Education

Date: 2025-10-18

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU

Pada 18 Oktober 2025, Free Malaysia Today menerbitkan rencana pendapat oleh guru-guru barisan hadapan yang menggambarkan sistem persekolahan dalam kemerosotan yang jelas. Penceritaan mereka terus terang: pelajar menatal TikTok di bawah meja semasa pengajaran, membentak guru apabila ditegur, enggan bekerjasama dengan aktiviti kelas, dan menunjukkan sedikit atau tiada rasa ingin tahu tentang apa yang diajar.

Guru-guru menggambarkan perjuangan yang kalah — bukan terhadap pelajar, tetapi terhadap algoritma. Gelung dopamin TikTok telah menjadi pihak berkuasa sebenar bilik darjah. Dan secara struktur, guru tiada apa-apa untuk melawan: tiada pedagogi yang dikemas kini, tiada dasar pengurusan peranti, tiada sokongan kesihatan mental, dan tiada pengakuan institusi bahawa masalah itu wujud.

item.title: Malaysia's Schooling System in 'Decline' — Students Ruder, Less Curious, Teachers Overwhelmed
item.description:
Said by: FMT Opinion / Teachers

Category: Education

Date: 2025-10-18

📌 WHAT HAPPENED

On 18 October 2025, Free Malaysia Today published an opinion piece by frontline teachers describing a schooling system in visible decline. The accounts were blunt: students scrolling TikTok under desks during lessons, snapping back at teachers when corrected, refusing to cooperate with classroom activities, and showing little to no curiosity about what’s being taught.

Teachers described fighting a losing battle — not against students, but against the algorithm. TikTok’s dopamine loop has become the real classroom authority. And structurally, teachers have nothing to fight back with: no updated pedagogy, no device management policy, no mental health support, and no institutional acknowledgment that the problem even exists.

item.description:

Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek menghadapi kritikan terbuka dari pelbagai pihak — termasuk rakan gabungannya sendiri, Menteri Sumber Asli Nik Nazmi, yang secara terbuka menyatakan bahawa ‘krisis pendidikan berpunca daripada sistem yang gagalkan kedua-dua guru dan pelajar.’ Dengan 7,681 kes buli pada 2024 (naik 17%), 10,160 pelajar tidak hadir SPM, kadar kegagalan matematik 25%, dan 30% calon SPM gagal sekurang-kurangnya satu subjek, sistem ini dalam keruntuhan.

item.title: Education Minister Under Fire — 'System Failed Both Teachers and Students' Says Own PH Minister
item.description:
Said by: Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad / Fadhlina Sidek (Education Minister)

Category: Education

Date: 2025-10-17

📌 What Happened

Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek faced open criticism from multiple quarters — including her own coalition colleague, Natural Resources Minister Nik Nazmi, who publicly stated that the ’education crisis stems from a system that failed both teachers and students.’ With 7,681 bullying cases in 2024 (up 17%), 10,160 SPM no-shows, 25% math failure rates, and 30% of SPM candidates failing at least one subject, the system is in freefall.

item.title: [BM] Sekolah Cina Dan Tamil Dijadikan Bola Politik Setiap Bajet — Dijanjikan Jutaan, Diberikan Sedikit
item.description:
Said by: Dong Zong / Tamil Foundation / MCA / MIC

Category: Education

Date: 2025-10-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Setiap kitaran bajet Malaysia menghasilkan teater yang sama: komuniti sekolah Cina dan Tamil melobi terdesak untuk dana penyelenggaraan, pembinaan dan pembangunan. Ahli politik mengumumkan peruntukan dengan penuh kemeriahan. Kemudian pencairan sebenar tidak mencukupi, tertangguh, atau disertakan syarat yang mengehadkan penggunaan. Kitaran ini berulang setiap tahun, dengan komuniti bukan Melayu menunjukkan rasa syukur terhadap peruntukan yang tidak memadai.

item.title: Chinese and Tamil Schools Used as Political Football Every Budget — Promised Millions, Delivered Scraps
item.description:
Said by: Dong Zong / Tamil Foundation / MCA / MIC

Category: Education

Date: 2025-10-01

📌 What Happened

Every Malaysian budget cycle produces the same theatre: Chinese and Tamil school communities lobby desperately for maintenance, construction, and development funds. Politicians announce allocations with fanfare. Then the actual disbursement falls short, is delayed, or comes with conditions that limit use. The cycle repeats annually, with non-Malay communities performing gratitude for inadequate allocations.

item.title: [BM] Bajet Pendidikan Tinggi Terus Menyusut — Dari 6.8% Pada 2010 Kepada Hanya 4.3% Pada 2025
item.description:
Said by: New Mandala / Academic Analysis

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Bajet pendidikan tinggi Malaysia telah jatuh dari 6.8% daripada jumlah bajet negara pada 2010 kepada hanya 4.3% pada 2025, dengan titik terendah pada 3.9% pada 2023. Sementara itu, enrolmen tertiari berada pada hanya 42.57% — jauh di bawah 93% Singapura dan purata global 51.98%. Analisis akademik menggambarkan “jurang yang semakin melebar antara wacana reformis dan komitmen kewangan sebenar” terhadap pendidikan di bawah PH.

item.title: [BM] Enrolmen Tertiari Malaysia Pada 42.57% — Di Bawah Purata Global, Jauh Ketinggalan 93% Singapura
item.description:
Said by: Academic Research / UNESCO Data

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

Hanya 42.57% rakyat Malaysia yang layak mendaftar dalam pendidikan tertiari — di bawah purata global 51.98%. Singapura pada 93%, AS pada 88%. Lebih 10,000 pelajar SPM (2.6%) tidak menduduki peperiksaan.

item.title: [BM] Jurang Digital Berterusan — Komuniti Luar Bandar Masih Tanpa Internet Yang Boleh Dipercayai Sementara Kerajaan Bercakap 5G
item.description:
Said by: MCMC / Rural Development Ministry

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Sehingga awal 2025, berjuta-juta rakyat Malaysia di kawasan luar bandar Sabah, Sarawak dan pantai timur Semenanjung Malaysia masih tidak mempunyai akses internet yang boleh dipercayai. Sementara kerajaan membelanjakan berbilion untuk bencana rangkaian dwi 5G DNB lawan Telekom Malaysia, program JENDELA untuk menambah baik infrastruktur digital asas menghadapi kelewatan dan jurang liputan. Pelajar di sekolah luar bandar sangat terpinggir semasa pembelajaran jarak jauh COVID-19, dan jurang digital tidak mengecil secara bermakna sejak itu. Data SKMM sendiri menunjukkan jurang ketersambungan antara kawasan bandar dan luar bandar kekal ketara, dengan banyak sekolah luar bandar bergantung kepada sambungan satelit yang tidak stabil atau tiada ketersambungan langsung.

item.title: [BM] Kekurangan Guru Di Sekolah Luar Bandar — Anak Kampung Dapat Pendidikan Kelas Kedua
item.description:
Said by: Education Ministry / NUTP

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Sekolah luar bandar di seluruh Malaysia menghadapi kekurangan guru kronik dalam matematik, sains, dan bahasa Inggeris — tiga mata pelajaran paling kritikal untuk daya saing ekonomi. Komuniti orang asli di Sabah, Sarawak, dan penempatan Orang Asli menghadapi jurang paling teruk, dengan sesetengah sekolah langsung tiada guru berkelayakan untuk mata pelajaran utama. Kesatuan Perkhidmatan Perguruan Kebangsaan (NUTP) telah berulang kali membangkitkan isu ini. Kementerian Pendidikan mengakui kekurangan tetapi tidak melaksanakan pembaharuan struktur.

item.title: [BM] Krisis Pinjaman PTPTN — Berjuta Berhutang Berbilion, Kadar Bayaran Balik Teruk, Graduan Terperangkap Dalam Hutang
item.description:
Said by: PTPTN / Auditor General Reports

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Perbadanan Tabung Pendidikan Tinggi Nasional (PTPTN) menghadapi krisis bayaran balik yang kronik, dengan berbilion ringgit pinjaman tertunggak dan kadar bayaran balik yang secara konsisten gagal mencapai sasaran. Berjuta graduan Malaysia menanggung hutang PTPTN yang menghadkan keupayaan mereka untuk menyimpan, melabur, atau membeli rumah. Kelestarian dana itu dipersoalkan tanpa reformasi besar.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Hutang PTPTN mewujudkan perangkap kemiskinan antara generasi: graduan memasuki tenaga kerja sudah berhutang, menghadapi ekonomi dengan pengangguran belia 12.28%, memperoleh gaji yang hampir tidak menanggung kos sara hidup (gaji minimum RM1,500), dan perlu membayar balik pinjaman pelajar sambil membina kehidupan. Ramai tidak mampu — sebab itulah kadar bayaran balik begitu rendah. Kitaran ini memakan dirinya sendiri: pendidikan tidak mampu → hutang → gaji rendah → tidak mampu bayar balik → isu kelayakan kredit → tidak mampu dapatkan gadai janji → status penyewa kekal.

item.title: Digital Divide Persists — Rural Communities Still Without Reliable Internet While Government Talks 5G
item.description:
Said by: MCMC / Rural Development Ministry

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: As of early 2025, millions of Malaysians in rural Sabah, Sarawak, and the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia still lack reliable internet access. While the government spent billions on the 5G DNB versus Telekom Malaysia dual-network fiasco, the JENDELA programme to improve basic digital infrastructure faced delays and coverage gaps. Students in rural schools were severely disadvantaged during COVID-19 distance learning, and the digital divide has not meaningfully narrowed since. MCMC’s own data shows connectivity gaps between urban and rural areas remain significant, with many rural schools relying on unstable satellite connections or no connectivity at all.

item.title: Higher Education Budget Keeps Shrinking — From 6.8% in 2010 to Just 4.3% in 2025
item.description:
Said by: New Mandala / Academic Analysis

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Malaysia’s higher education budget has dropped from 6.8% of the total national budget in 2010 to just 4.3% in 2025, with the lowest point at 3.9% in 2023. Meanwhile, tertiary enrollment stands at only 42.57% — far below Singapore’s 93% and the global average of 51.98%. Academic analysis describes a “widening disjuncture between reformist discourse and actual financial commitment” to education under PH. While the government talks about the knowledge economy and human capital development, the budget tells a different story.

item.title: Malaysia Tertiary Enrollment at 42.57% — Below Global Average, Far Behind Singapore's 93%
item.description:
Said by: Academic Research / UNESCO Data

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

Only 42.57% of eligible Malaysians enrolled in tertiary education — below global average of 51.98%. Singapore at 93%, US at 88%. Over 10,000 SPM students (2.6%) didn’t even sit for the exam.

item.title: PTPTN Loan Crisis — Millions Owe Billions, Repayment Rates Abysmal, Graduates Trapped in Debt
item.description:
Said by: PTPTN / Auditor General Reports

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) faces a chronic repayment crisis, with billions of ringgit in outstanding loans and repayment rates that consistently fall short of targets. Millions of Malaysian graduates carry PTPTN debt that limits their ability to save, invest, or purchase homes. The fund’s sustainability is questionable without major reform.

🔥 Why It Matters

PTPTN debt creates a generational poverty trap: graduates enter the workforce already indebted, face an economy with 12.28% youth unemployment, earn wages that barely cover living costs (RM1,500 minimum wage), and must somehow repay student loans while building a life. Many can’t — which is why repayment rates are so low. The cycle feeds itself: unaffordable education → debt → low wages → inability to repay → creditworthiness issues → inability to get mortgages → permanent renter status.

item.title: Teacher Shortage in Rural Schools — Kids in Kampungs Get Second-Class Education
item.description:
Said by: Education Ministry / NUTP

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Rural schools across Malaysia face chronic teacher shortages in mathematics, science, and English — the three subjects most critical for economic competitiveness. Indigenous communities in Sabah, Sarawak, and Orang Asli settlements face the worst gaps, with some schools lacking qualified teachers entirely for key subjects. The National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP) has repeatedly raised the issue. The Education Ministry acknowledges the shortage but has not implemented structural reforms to address it.

item.title: [BM] Skor PISA Runtuh — Malaysia Hilang 1.6 TAHUN Pembelajaran, Kini 8 Tahun Di Belakang Singapura Dalam Matematik
item.description:
Said by: OECD PISA 2022 Report / ISIS Malaysia Analysis

Category: Education

Date: 2024-12-06

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Laporan PISA 2022, dikeluarkan pada Disember 2024, mendedahkan Malaysia mengalami antara lima penurunan terbesar di dunia merentas ketiga-tiga subjek. Matematik jatuh 31 mata (440 kepada 409), bacaan turun 27 mata (415 kepada 388), dan sains merosot 22 mata (438 kepada 416). ISIS Malaysia menganggarkan ini setara dengan 1.6 tahun pembelajaran yang hilang dalam matematik sahaja. 59% pelajar Malaysia kini di bawah kecekapan asas dalam matematik — naik daripada 41%. Hanya 1% pelajar Malaysia mencapai kecekapan tinggi. Jurang sosioekonomi semakin melebar, dengan pelajar kaya mengatasi pelajar kurang berkemampuan sebanyak 82 mata.

item.title: PISA Scores Collapse — Malaysia Loses 1.6 YEARS of Learning, Now 8 Years Behind Singapore in Math
item.description:
Said by: OECD PISA 2022 Report / ISIS Malaysia Analysis

Category: Education

Date: 2024-12-06

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: The 2022 PISA report, released in December 2024, revealed Malaysia suffered among the top five largest declines globally across all three subjects. Mathematics dropped 31 points (440 to 409), reading fell 27 points (415 to 388), and science declined 22 points (438 to 416). ISIS Malaysia estimated this equates to 1.6 years of lost learning in mathematics alone. 59% of Malaysian students are now below basic proficiency in math — up from 41%. Only 1% of Malaysian students achieved high proficiency. The socioeconomic gap is widening, with wealthy students outperforming disadvantaged ones by 82 points.

item.title: [BM] 30% Calon SPM GAGAL Sekurang-kurangnya Satu Mata Pelajaran — Gred Lulus 20% Dalam Matematik Bukan Pendidikan, Ia Pembohongan
item.description:
Said by: Education Ministry Data / Independent Analysis

Category: Education

Date: 2024-05-27

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Dalam keputusan SPM 2023 yang dikeluarkan pada Mei 2024, kira-kira 30% calon gagal sekurang-kurangnya satu mata pelajaran. Matematik mempunyai kadar kegagalan tertinggi pada 25.9%, diikuti sains pada 25%. Mata pelajaran terbaik adalah Quran dan Sunnah pada 84%. Laporan menunjukkan ambang lulus untuk matematik mungkin serendah 20% — bermakna pelajar yang mendapat 4 daripada 5 soalan salah masih “lulus.” Kerajaan sebelum ini telah memansuhkan peperiksaan UPSR (Tahun 6) dan PMR (Tahun 9), menghapuskan satu-satunya pusat pemeriksaan diagnostik yang boleh mengenal pasti pelajar yang bergelut awal.

item.title: 30% of SPM Candidates FAIL At Least One Subject — A Pass Grade of 20% in Math Is Not Education, It's a Lie
item.description:
Said by: Education Ministry Data / Independent Analysis

Category: Education

Date: 2024-05-27

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: In SPM 2023 results released in May 2024, approximately 30% of candidates failed at least one subject. Mathematics had the highest failure rate at 25.9%, followed by science at 25%. The best-performing subject was Quran and Sunnah at 84%. Reports indicate the pass threshold for mathematics may be as low as 20% — meaning a student who gets 4 out of 5 questions wrong still “passes.” The government had previously abolished UPSR (Year 6) and PMR (Year 9) examinations, removing the only diagnostic checkpoints that could identify struggling students early.

item.title: [BM] Lebih 10,000 Pelajar SPM Langsung Tidak Menduduki Peperiksaan — Sistem Pendidikan Kehilangan Pelajar
item.description:
Said by: Education Ministry / DOSM

Category: Education

Date: 2024-03-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Lebih 10,160 calon SPM yang berdaftar — 2.6% daripada jumlah keseluruhan — tidak menduduki peperiksaan sekolah terpenting Malaysia pada 2023. Ini bukan ralat pembundaran; ia mewakili lebih sepuluh ribu anak muda Malaysia yang meninggalkan sistem pendidikan sepenuhnya. Digabungkan dengan kadar kemasukan pengajian tinggi hanya 42.57% (berbanding 93% Singapura dan purata global 51.98%), pengangguran belia kekal pada 12.28%, peruntukan bajet pendidikan tinggi yang jatuh dari 6.8% pada 2010 kepada 4.3% pada 2025, dan 7,681 kes buli yang dilaporkan, sistem ini kehilangan pelajar di setiap peringkat.

item.title: Over 10,000 SPM Students Didn't Even Sit for the Exam — Education System Haemorrhaging
item.description:
Said by: Education Ministry / DOSM

Category: Education

Date: 2024-03-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: More than 10,160 registered SPM candidates — 2.6% of the total — did not sit for Malaysia’s most important school examination in 2023. This is not a rounding error; it represents over ten thousand young Malaysians who disengaged from the education system entirely. Combined with a tertiary enrollment rate of just 42.57% (versus Singapore’s 93% and the global average of 51.98%), youth unemployment stuck at 12.28%, a higher education budget share that dropped from 6.8% in 2010 to 4.3% in 2025, and 7,681 reported bullying cases, the system is haemorrhaging students at every level.

item.title: [BM] Skor PISA Malaysia Merosot Paling Teruk Di Kalangan Negara Asia Tenggara — Anwar Kata 'Tidak Boleh Nafikan'
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2024-01-15

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Keputusan PISA 2022 Malaysia — mengukur kualiti pendidikan pelajar berumur 15 tahun — menunjukkan kemerosotan terbesar di kalangan semua negara Asia Tenggara yang diuji. Skor jatuh merentas matematik, sains, dan bacaan. Anwar merespons dengan mengatakan Malaysia “mesti mengetahui keadaan sebenar dan tidak boleh dalam keadaan menafikan.” Menteri Pendidikan mengakui sistem itu “mengecewakan guru dan pelajar.” CNA melaporkan bahawa politik — terutamanya ketegangan antara keperluan bahasa Melayu dan kecekapan bahasa Inggeris — berada di sebalik kesukaran reformasi pendidikan. Tiga tahun kemudian, pakar mengatakan tiada apa yang berubah di lapangan.

item.title: Malaysia's PISA Scores Decline Most Among Southeast Asian Countries — Anwar Says 'Cannot Be in Denial'
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Education

Date: 2024-01-15

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Malaysia’s 2022 PISA results — measuring education quality among 15-year-olds — showed the biggest decline among all Southeast Asian countries tested. Scores dropped across mathematics, science, and reading. Anwar responded by saying Malaysia “must know the state of our affairs and cannot be in a state of denial.” The Education Minister admitted the system “failed both teachers and students.” CNA reported that politics — particularly the tension between Malay language requirements and English proficiency — is behind the difficulty of education reform. Three years later, experts say nothing has changed on the ground.
